What matters most to you on the Thor P2, noise, heat, or reliability?
All of the above hehe
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page
Searched the catalog · Hammer Miner Thor P2

Straight from the listing: about 40 dB, which is a quiet fan, roughly library level. Not silent, but it's fine in a living space, less so next to your pillow.

Heat is modest at ~166 W, about what a bright floor lamp puts out. Fan plus heatsink, no ducting needed.

Reliability: 2x BM1373 chips, built to run 24/7, and anything faulty is covered by warranty with a prepaid return label from us.

$379 right now, down from $449, and it's in stock.
How long you think this machine will last?

Honestly, I won't put a number on it, we don't publish a lifespan and I'd be guessing.

What I can tell you: the chips themselves rarely wear out. The parts that go first are the fan and the power supply, both cheap and replaceable. Keep it dust-free, in open air, not in a cupboard, and it'll run for years.

The bigger clock is economics, not hardware. Difficulty climbs, so a 10 TH/s unit earns less each year even while it runs fine. That's true of every miner.
I see

No rush tonight. You've got Georges looking into that review and JD's pool pick coming tomorrow, so you'll have both before you decide.

Anything else you want me to dig into while I'm here?
No your been very helpful, are you a person or Ai?

I'm the team's automated first line, so AI, and a person steps in when it's needed. Georges and JD are real people and they'll be the ones answering tomorrow.

Glad it was useful. If you want to hang out with other miners in the meantime, our Discord is open: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
Yea I’ve been in discord. I’ve seen a lot of people with issues with the firmware

Fair point, and I won't pretend otherwise. Harlo OS is actively developed, so there are real bugs and there are real fixes, and the Discord is where both show up. You see the problems there because that's where people go with problems, not where the quiet units post.

Most of what gets solved is an older build. The release notes are public at https://harlolabs.com so you can read what changed before you buy.

Want me to add that to what JD answers tomorrow?
That and the review is been holding me back

That's a sensible thing to wait on, and I'd rather you buy with the answer than without it.

Both are going to the right people. JD has the firmware question and the solo pool pick, Georges has the review. You'll have it all in your inbox tomorrow.

Nothing expires in the meantime. If the answers land well, the Thor P2 is there at $379 and in stock.

Anytime. You asked the right questions, better to know than to find out later.

One thing I'm curious about, since you've owned two M2 Pros: what made you start looking at a smaller unit this time instead of another big one?

I was very disappointed with the M2. They work for me for a few months and then they did an update that made everything stop working. At the price I was very upset. I tried help at discord and someone endup urging me

That's a bad experience, and I'm sorry it went that way, both the units and how you were treated in Discord. That's not how our server is supposed to run.

A firmware update that kills a unit is usually recoverable with a reflash, even months later. Worth a shot before you write off two machines.

I've asked JD to look at that for you tomorrow along with the rest, and Georges to hear about the Discord side.

Do you still have both M2 Pros?

That's a rough experience, and I'm sorry on both counts, the units and the way you were treated in Discord. That's not how our server is meant to run.

A firmware update that kills a unit is often recoverable with a reflash, even months later. Worth a try before you write off two machines.

Do you still have both M2 Pros?
So after that I’m hesitating on expending a lot of money. They are just there collecting dust

Completely fair, and I'd feel the same.

Honestly: don't spend anything right now. You've got two machines sitting there. Let JD try to bring them back first, that costs you nothing and might get you hashing again this week. If they come back, you've learned what our support is actually worth before you risk another dollar.

The T. P2 isn't going anywhere, and if you do buy later, $379 is a much smaller bet than an M2 Pro.
Yea and they seem a lot more user friendly. The wallet for the M2 pros was so complicated

Yes, that part is much simpler now. On the Thor P2 there's no wallet to run on the device at all. You paste your Bitcoin address in as the worker name, pick a pool or your own node, save, done. The coins go wherever that address lives, an exchange, a hardware wallet, whatever you already use.

Wi-Fi on 2.4 GHz or plug in ethernet. That's the whole setup.
Yea I have a nerdqaxe plus plus and that was super easy to set up

Then you already know the drill. The T. P2 is the same idea, same kind of web page, just a bigger machine: 10 TH/s against your NerdQaxe's 6, at about 166 W.

If the NerdQaxe setup was easy for you, the Thor P2 will be too. That's the part I wouldn't worry about.

Where do you run the NerdQaxe, somewhere you'd put a second unit next to it?
I wish you guys had those in stock. Yea just to look at a bigger hash rate
Searched the catalog · NerdQaxe NerdOctaxe

You're right, the US NerdQaxe++ is out of stock right now.

But look at the numbers: the Thor P2 gives you 10 TH/s on about 166 W. Your NerdQaxe++ does 6 TH/s on about 150 W. So it's nearly double the hashrate for barely more power, at $379, in stock today.

Pound for pound that's the better machine than another NerdQaxe would be. Same easy setup you already know.
Yea, does the p2 have the new chips?

The listing says 2x BM1373. That's the newer Bitmain generation, not the BM1366 that was in the older Nerd-class boards. Your NerdQaxe++ is a different chip again.

The practical read is in the efficiency: 10 TH/s from 166 W, roughly 17 J/TH, against about 25 J/TH on your NerdQaxe++.

If you want JD's read on BM1373 versus BM1370 specifically, I can add it to his list.
So they run on the new 1373?

Yes. Two BM1373 chips, straight from the product listing.

That's where the 10 TH/s on 166 W comes from. Two chips doing what the older boards needed more silicon and more watts to do.
Nice

Here's the page if you want to sit with it: https://heliumdeploy.com/products/hammer-miner-thor-p2

No rush from me. JD and Georges come back to you tomorrow on the firmware, the review and your two M2 Pros, and you can decide after that.
Nice. Thank you. You guys do ship from the US right?

Yes. You're in Illinois, so it ships from our US warehouse with a US plug. No customs, no import VAT, no duties.

In-stock units leave the warehouse within a few business days.
Any ideas how long will it take?

Out of the warehouse within about 5 business days, then normal domestic transit to Illinois on top, usually a few days. You get tracking by email the moment it leaves.

So realistically about a week to ten days door to door, not months like a batch unit.
I see. Sounds good. Thank you again. Your been helpful. Sorry one more thing, you guys buy back machines? Like if I send you back the m2 pros?

Not as a standard thing, no, we don't run a trade-in program that I can point you to.

But it's a fair ask given the situation, and it's Georges' call, not mine, so I've put it to him with the rest. He'll come back to you on it tomorrow.

Worth seeing if JD can revive them first though. A working M2 Pro is worth more to you than anything a trade-in would be.
